audience.text: Python developers who need to parse, inspect, modify, and serialize HTML documents using WHATWG DOM and CSSOM APIs without requiring a full browser environment.

capabilities.text: Parse HTML strings, bytes, fragments, and files into a DOM document with `HTMLDocument.parse()`, `HTMLDocument.parse_fragment()`, and `HTMLDocument.load()`.
capabilities.title: Parse HTML into a DOM tree

capabilities.text: Build, inspect, and mutate DOM trees using `Document.create_element()`, `append_child()`, attribute manipulation, and query helpers like `get_element_by_id()` and `get_elements_by_tag_name()`.
capabilities.title: Query and mutate DOM elements

capabilities.text: Match CSS selectors and stylesheets against elements and resolve the cascade with `Element.get_computed_style()` and the CSSOM surface including `CSSStyleSheet`, `CSSStyleRule`, and `CSSMediaRule`.
capabilities.title: Apply CSS and resolve computed styles

capabilities.text: Serialize complete documents, fragments, and individual elements back to an HTML string with the `serialise()` function or `XMLSerializer`.
capabilities.title: Serialize HTML output

capabilities.text: Validate and manipulate URLs with `URL`, read and edit query strings with `URLSearchParams`, and detect byte-stream character encodings with `detect_encoding()`.
capabilities.title: Handle URLs and query parameters

capabilities.text: Execute JavaScript against a parsed DOM through `JSContext`, an optional QuickJS-backed bridge exposing read-only DOM proxies to script code.
capabilities.title: Execute JavaScript against the DOM

limitations.text: CSS selector matching supports the core CSS Selectors Level 3 grammar, but several dynamic and legacy pseudo-classes are out of scope and raise `NotImplementedError` in the matcher and parser.
Form constraint validation (validity-state computation) and `HTMLImageElement.decode()` are present on the API surface but not yet implemented.
The library builds internal layout structures but does not yet expose a public API for rendering documents to an image or PDF.
JavaScript execution (`JSContext`) requires the optional `quickjs` extra and exposes a read-only DOM proxy to script code; its dynamic `import()` bridge is not implemented.

problems_solved.text: Parse HTML strings, bytes, fragments, and files into a DOM document using `HTMLDocument.parse()`, `HTMLDocument.parse_fragment()`, and `HTMLDocument.load()`.
Apply CSS stylesheets and resolve computed styles for elements using the CSSOM surface including `CSSStyleSheet`, `CSSStyleRule`, and `get_computed_style()`.
Match CSS selectors and query elements by ID, tag name, class name, and selector-oriented helpers such as `get_element_by_id()` and `get_elements_by_tag_name()`.
Execute JavaScript against a parsed DOM through `JSContext`, an optional QuickJS-backed bridge exposing read-only DOM proxies to script code.

product_summary.text: Aspose.HTML FOSS for Python is a free, open-source, MIT-licensed Python library for parsing HTML into a standards-based DOM tree, applying CSS, and serializing markup back out.

uncertainties: The exact set of unimplemented pseudo-classes and pseudo-elements is not explicitly listed in the facts.
The specific behavior of `HTMLImageElement.decode()` and form constraint validation when called is not documented in the facts.
The scope of the read-only DOM proxy exposed to JavaScript is not fully detailed in the facts.

workflows.name: Parse and modify HTML
workflows.text: Parse HTML strings into a DOM tree, create and append new elements, update text content, and serialize the result back to HTML using `serialise()`.

workflows.name: Apply and resolve CSS
workflows.text: Attach a `CSSStyleSheet` to a document, match selectors, and resolve computed styles for elements using `get_computed_style()`.

workflows.name: Work with URLs and query parameters
workflows.text: Parse and manipulate URLs and query strings using `URL` and `URLSearchParams`.

workflows.name: Detect character encoding
workflows.text: Detect character encoding from byte streams using `detect_encoding()` with BOM and content sniffing support.

workflows.name: Tokenize HTML directly
workflows.text: Drive the tokenizer directly using `Tokenizer` and inspect tokens such as `StartTagToken` and `CommentToken`.

workflows.name: Build and traverse DOM trees
workflows.text: Create elements with `Document.create_element()`, append children, and traverse the tree using `TreeWalker`, `NodeIterator`, and `Range`.
